name: Portability Regulation
evidence_rating: thin: one Commission review backed by surveys and self-reported provider evidence; no independent or causal studies
summary: The Portability Regulation lets people use their paid streaming, music and gaming subscriptions when travelling in other EU countries. The Commission's 2022 review found it works well: about a third of subscribers had used their services abroad, few complained, and providers and rightholders reported only minor costs, though some services still cap how long you can use them abroad. No independent study has measured its economic effects.

indicators.objective: The proposal has no financial statement indicators; the memorandum only promised two-phase monitoring with attention to SMEs and consumers. The Commission reported on application in SWD(2022) 173 (Article 10 review)

indicators.indicator: Potential users of portability of paid subscriptions: 29 million (5.7% of EU consumers) in 2015, rising to about 72 million (14%) by 2020
indicators.evidence: Partially measured: Flash Eurobarometer (Feb 2019) found 32% of subscribers (49% of those who travelled) had tried to use their service in another Member State; providers report cross-border users are under 5% of their subscribers; COVID-19 travel restrictions reduced use. No headcount comparable to the forecast.

indicators.indicator: Consumer awareness and satisfaction with portability
indicators.evidence: Measured once: 52% of respondents aware of portability; 58% of users satisfied (2019). Over 80% of surveyed providers and 23 of 32 consumer bodies received no complaints.

indicators.indicator: Compliance and implementation costs for providers, in particular SMEs
indicators.evidence: Survey-based: music, e-book and games providers already offered portability and faced no significant cost; audiovisual and sports providers had to adapt verification and infrastructure, costs reported as minor; SMEs found residence verification and data-protection compliance challenging. Some non-compliance: 10 providers limit portability to periods of 14 days to one year; some small providers unaware of the rules. No cost figures.

indicators.indicator: No significant negative effect on licensing value / rightholder revenues
indicators.evidence: Study found no significant impact on rightholders' overall revenues (self-reported; no quantitative analysis).

literature.citation: European Commission (2015), Impact Assessment accompanying the proposal for a Regulation to ensure the cross-border portability of online content services in the internal market, SWD(2015) 270
literature.title: Impact Assessment accompanying the proposal for a Regulation to ensure the cross-border portability of online content services in the internal market
literature.headline: Estimated 29 million potential users of portability of paid subscriptions (5.7% of EU consumers), forecast to reach about 72 million (14%) by 2020; costs for providers expected to be limited
literature.summary_plain: The Commission estimated that around 29 million Europeans could benefit from taking their paid streaming subscriptions abroad, rising to about 72 million by 2020.

literature.citation: European Commission (2022), Report on the application of Regulation (EU) 2017/1128 on cross-border portability of online content services in the internal market, SWD(2022) 173
literature.title: Report on the application of Regulation (EU) 2017/1128 on cross-border portability of online content services in the internal market
literature.method: review (synthesis of survey, Eurobarometer and stakeholder evidence)
literature.outcomes: consumer use and satisfaction; provider compliance; rightholder revenues
literature.headline: Regulation 'has proven to function well overall'; 32% of subscribers had used portability abroad, 58% of users satisfied; very few complaints; no significant revenue loss for rightholders reported; some non-compliance (time limits, too many verification means, small providers not offering portability)
literature.summary_plain: The Commission's 2022 review concluded the rules work well: about a third of subscribers had used their services abroad, few complained, and rightholders reported no significant revenue loss, though some providers still restrict portability.

literature.citation: Visionary Analytics with Kantar Public (for DG CNECT) (2022), Study on the Portability Regulation - Final report (SMART 2019/0024), European Commission, DG CNECT
literature.authors: Visionary Analytics with Kantar Public (for DG CNECT)
literature.title: Study on the Portability Regulation - Final report (SMART 2019/0024)
literature.method: surveys (62 providers, 40 consumer bodies), mystery shopping of 39 services, 63 interviews, case studies
literature.headline: Overwhelming majority of providers apply the Regulation; music, e-book and games sectors faced no significant costs; audiovisual and sports providers made changes with mostly minor costs; 10 providers limit temporary presence to 14 days-1 year; cross-border users under 5% of each provider's subscribers
literature.summary_plain: An evaluation study for the Commission found most services comply at small cost, but ten limit how long subscribers can use them abroad and some small providers ignore the rules.
literature.verified: full text read (abstract and summary sections)

literature.citation: European Commission (Kantar) (2019), Flash Eurobarometer 477a: Accessing content online and cross-border portability of online content services, Flash Eurobarometer 477a
literature.title: Flash Eurobarometer 477a: Accessing content online and cross-border portability of online content services
literature.headline: 52% aware of portability; 32% of subscribers had tried to access services while in another Member State; 58% of users satisfied
literature.summary_plain: A 2019 EU-wide survey found half of Europeans knew about the portability right and most of those who used it were satisfied.
literature.verified: page summary via Commission report (figures as cited in SWD(2022) 173)

literature.citation: European Audiovisual Observatory (2019), First feedback from the implementation of the Portability Regulation by free online video services, European Audiovisual Observatory (Council of Europe)
literature.title: First feedback from the implementation of the Portability Regulation by free online video services
literature.method: descriptive survey of free online video services
literature.outcomes: voluntary uptake of portability by free services
literature.headline: Of 13 free online video services in the sample, 4 had implemented portability, 2 were implementing and 7 considering; uptake led by public broadcasters; mandatory login and verification costs deter others
literature.summary_plain: Few free streaming services (mostly public broadcasters) had chosen to offer portability by 2019, citing login and verification costs.
